text.p: Swiss escalator and elevator maker Schindler Holding AG said it still expects 1997 profits to rise to around 160 million Swiss francs, excluding non-recurring costs of at least 25 million Swiss francs.

Schindler's annual report released today reiterated expectations for 1997 that the company last voiced on March 10, when it reported a 1996 net profit of 88.5 million Swiss francs after 78.5 million the year before.
Schindler said it expected continued growth in Asia's elevator and escalator market and a slight rebound in North America and Latin America.
It said there was no sign of improvement in demand or prices in most European markets but that new products this spring were expected to boost sales.
It also expected productivity in its European group companies to improve on a sustained basis.

"In view of the scenario outlined above -- assuming stable foreign exchange and economic baseline conditions -- and on the basis of positive results generated in 1996, Schindler is still aiming for a 1997 profitability level on par with 1993/94, i.e. about 160 million (Swiss francs), not counting non-recurring costs of at least 25 million," it said.
Alfred Spoerri, chief financial officer, said the 25 million was an accurate estimate of the total for restructuring costs the current 1997 year.
"From today's point of view it is a realistic estimate," Spoerri told reporters before today's news conference.
Spoerri declined to say anything specific about business at the start of the year.
"If we still stick to the 1997 forecast, then obviously there are no surprises for us (in the start of the year)," he said.
